$comment: The map of interop scenarios: every place where two implementations of the decentralized trust graph can meet. Not a ladder; scenarios have no order. Each scenario names its origin, what a project brings to take part (requires) and what has to happen between two projects for the scenario to count (done). A project's status at a scenario says how far it meets the requirements and scenarios at evidence; whether the row was written by the project or compiled from its public sources is provenance.kind; whether the scenario was shown between two projects follows only from a passing scenario result. Whoever adds a scenario decides that it belongs; its origin names where it comes from. A candidate line is an open question about the scenario itself. Scenarios with derivedFrom get a project's status filled in by the build from its detail fields (credentials, messaging, replication, trustTaskUse) where the project itself said no more than stated; the result is marked derived.

layers.title: The person
layers.asks: Who is this, across devices and apps?

layers.title: Two people
layers.asks: Can two people on two apps connect and talk to each other?

layers.title: Wire and documents
layers.asks: Does a sealed message arrive, and does the other side read what arrives?

layers.title: Membership
layers.asks: Who says someone belongs, and who reads it?

layers.title: Shared state
layers.asks: Can several apps hold the same group data, offline too and after a lost device?

layers.title: Networks
layers.asks: How do communities recognise one another?

scenarios.title: Identifier resolution across apps
scenarios.asks: Each side resolves the other's DID method and finds its keys.
requires: Both sides: an identifier under a DID method, and signatures with a key the DID resolves to
Each side: resolves the other side's DID method
scenarios.done: Each side verifies a signature the other side made under its DID, using keys from its own resolution of that DID.

scenarios.title: Several devices, one person
scenarios.asks: A person's devices act for the same person toward other apps, and a lost or restored device does not break the relationship.
requires: Person side: several devices under one person, each with a key of its own
Counterpart app: a relationship with the person, not with one device
scenarios.done: The counterpart app treats a person's second device as the same relationship, and a restored device continues it without a new ceremony.

scenarios.title: Use your credentials in several apps
scenarios.asks: A person uses the same relationship and membership credentials in two apps at once; moving from one app to another is the case where the first one is no longer used.
requires: First app: hands the person's credentials to the second app, together with access to a key of the person (shared, or a key of its own under the same person)
Second app: imports them, verifies each one (vrc-verify, membership-statement) and can act as their holder
scenarios.done: Credentials from one app are usable in another: they verify there, the person sees their contacts and memberships in both apps, and both apps keep working.
scenarios.origin: Weave deck, Level 0b (app change with VRCs and VMCs), read as concurrent use

scenarios.title: Contact ceremony between apps
scenarios.asks: Two people on different apps connect through one QR-code ceremony and both end with a credential the other app reads.
requires: Both apps: the same ceremony, run from one definition in the DTGWG ceremony format, one app as the displaying side and one as the scanning side
Both apps: issue and verify the credential the ceremony ends with (vrc-verify)
scenarios.done: Two people on different apps run one QR-code ceremony and each holds a credential the other app verifies.
scenarios.origin: Weave one-pager (QR-code contact ceremonies between apps); proposed as a level by rltp; definition format from the DTGWG Trust Ceremonies task force

scenarios.title: Verify another app's relationship credential
scenarios.asks: A relationship credential issued in one app verifies in another; no transport needed, a file is enough.
requires: Each side: issues a DTG RelationshipCredential with a proof from the credentials vocabulary
Each side: resolves the other side's DID method (did-resolution)
scenarios.done: Each side verifies proof, context and issuer scope of a relationship credential the other side issued.

scenarios.title: Direct message between apps
scenarios.asks: Two connected people on two different apps exchange a message each way, as a document both read.
requires: Both apps: a relationship between the two people (contact-ceremony, or any ceremony both apps accept)
Both apps: the same message document type, carrying a pairwise proof (a MAC or an equivalent construction) rather than a transferable signature
Both apps: a path between them (same-carrier or cross-carrier)
scenarios.done: Each person sends one message from their app; the other app shows it in the conversation with that person, the reply arrives the same way, and a third party holding the envelope cannot show who wrote it. A procedure may run it with the sender offline when writing: the message arrives later and is still accepted as of its issue time.
scenarios.origin: Weave one-pager (messaging across apps); proposed as a level by rltp; deniability from rltp

scenarios.title: Delivery through one carrier
scenarios.asks: Two apps reach each other through the same mediator or relay.
requires: Both apps: speak the carrier's wire protocol (TSP for the VTI mediator) and have a relationship or an account at the same carrier; a passing run of tsp-conformance shows the wire side
Both apps: seal and open messages for the other side's identifier
scenarios.done: A sealed message from one app arrives at the other through one carrier and opens, in both directions.
scenarios.origin: tsp-conformance, VTI; wire conformance from OpenVTC tsp-conformance

scenarios.title: Delivery across carriers
scenarios.asks: Two parties at different mediators or relays still reach each other.
requires: Each app: reachable at a carrier of its own
The carriers: forward to one another, or one app reaches both
scenarios.done: A sealed message from one app at one carrier arrives at the other app at another carrier and opens, in both directions.

scenarios.title: Common document framework
scenarios.asks: Wire artifacts are Trust Task documents with type URI, schema and proof the other side can check.
requires: Each side: emits its wire artifacts as Trust Task documents with a type URI, a schema and a proof
Each side: parses foreign Trust Task documents, with a shared library or its own
scenarios.done: A document emitted by one app parses in the other as a Trust Task document and its proof verifies, even where the receiver does not know the type.
scenarios.origin: DTGWG Trust Tasks framework; document conformance (shared vectors and runner) from the Trust Tasks task force and the Weave one-pager

scenarios.title: Error and status answers
scenarios.asks: A receiver that cannot process a document answers in a form the sender reads.
requires: Receiving side: answers a document it cannot process with trust-task-error
Sending side: reads trust-task-error and shows it or acts on it
scenarios.done: One app sends a document the other cannot process; the answer is a trust-task-error the sender reads, and the sender's state afterwards matches the error.

scenarios.title: Membership statement another app reads
scenarios.asks: A community states who belongs in a form a wallet or another app holds and verifies.
requires: Community side: issues a statement of who belongs (a VMC or an equivalent document) under the community's identifier
Other app: verifies the statement and the issuer's authority over the community
scenarios.done: A membership statement issued in one app verifies in another, naming the person and the community.
scenarios.origin: Weave deck, Level 1a; also covers Weave Level 1b (one membership, several apps) once the statement verifies in two or more apps

scenarios.title: Sub-groups with their own credentials
scenarios.asks: A sub-group issues credentials of its own, and another app verifies them through the parent group.
requires: Community side: a sub-group with an identifier of its own, and a statement from the parent group that the sub-group belongs to it
Other app: verifies a sub-group credential together with the parent's statement
scenarios.done: Another app verifies a credential issued by a sub-group and that the parent group backs that sub-group.

scenarios.title: Interop with traditional tools
scenarios.asks: A group governed in the trust substrate is used by a conventional tool (calendar, forum, folder) that only asks who belongs.
requires: Group side: a membership statement or an authorization view that answers who belongs
Tool side: a conventional tool that grants access on that answer
scenarios.done: A conventional tool grants access to a group governed in the trust substrate, asking only who belongs.
scenarios.origin: Weave one-pager (how decentralized tools interoperate with traditional ones)

scenarios.title: Same group in two apps
scenarios.asks: Several apps read and write the same encrypted shared state of one community.
requires: Host side: a group whose shared state is encrypted under one group key agreement at the boundary (MLS 1.0, ciphersuite 0x0001), joinable by welcome or invitation
Joining side: a client of its own implementation that joins, reads and writes
scenarios.done: A client of one implementation joins a group hosted by another, reads the records already there and writes one the host reads back. A procedure may run it with the writer offline when writing: the record arrives later and the host accepts it as of its issue time.
scenarios.origin: Weave deck, Level 2a; one-pager (being in the same group in two different apps); key agreement at the boundary from rltp (E13)

scenarios.title: History for newcomers
scenarios.asks: A member admitted later reads what the group wrote before, as far as the group allows.
requires: Both sides: shared-room
Host side: keeps earlier epochs or keys for newcomers, as far as the group allows
scenarios.done: A member admitted later from the other app reads what the group wrote before the admission, within what the group allows, and nothing beyond.

scenarios.title: Recovery after a captured device
scenarios.asks: Removing a device ends its access to future group content on every app.
requires: Both sides: shared-room or key-agreement
Removing side: removes a device from the group and rotates the group key
scenarios.done: After one app removes a device, content written afterwards in either app does not open on that device.

scenarios.title: Registry lookup
scenarios.asks: Two communities recognise each other through a registry.
requires: Registry side: a registry that answers whether a community is recognised, as a Trust Task or an equivalent
Querying side: asks the registry before trusting a statement from a community it does not know
scenarios.done: One community accepts a statement from another it does not know because a registry both read recognises it.

scenarios.title: Networks of communities
scenarios.asks: A community recognises a member of a community it does not know, through a third community both know.
requires: Three communities: a statement of recognition from the third to each of the other two (registry-lookup or membership-statement)
Accepting side: follows the chain of recognition
scenarios.done: A community accepts a membership statement of a community it has no direct relation with, through one it has.

statusWords.stated: the project says so in its own public texts or code we could point at, read by someone else; the row has not been confirmed by the project
statusWords.runs: the project meets the requirements in code or a live service another project can exercise today; not yet a run between two projects
statusWords.vectors: byte-exact test vectors published, re-derivable by a shared runner, not yet exercised against another implementation
statusWords.open: the project knows the gap and says so
statusWords.n/a: the project does not aim at this scenario, with a reason

shown: A scenario counts as run between two projects only through a passing run of a procedure that covers it (or a partial run naming it). Project statuses never add up to a run.
